Marcus —

Thanks for the ping. I've reviewed MedHealth's redline and annotated our recommended positions (attached: RW_DPA_counter_20261003.docx). High-level:
1) SCCs: we can accept the substance of their SCC variant but need to insert our standard mapping language and limit the additional audit window they requested. Recommend we propose Redwood's SCC annex and add a short migration sentence.
2) Subprocessors: agree to quarterly bulletin + on-request detailed list. That satisfies most procurement asks while keeping operational overhead manageable.
3) HIPAA carve-outs: we need to be explicit that Redwood acts as a processor under the DPA and that customer remains responsible for covered entity obligations; offer BAAs on a case-by-case basis.
4) Warranty/Indemnity: push back on unlimited indemnity; propose a capped carve (see section 7 counter).

Routing/signature: propose DocuSign route with two internal signatories: VP Sales (Marcus) and Head of Legal (me). For exec-level exceptions (SLA/credit changes), escalate to CPO. I can prepare the DocuSign envelope once counters are agreed.

I've uploaded a SOC 2 evidence snapshot to our internal drive and included a summary file (SOC2_evidence_snapshot_link.txt) for their security review. Karthik — any compliance redlines to call out before I send the counter?

Best,
Priyom
Legal Operations
Attachment: RW_DPA_counter_20261003.docx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-03T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MedHealth DPA redline for review — SCC/HIPAA notes

Quick notes from infosec/compliance perspective:
- SCC variant: acceptable if we add AES-256 at-rest language and limit third-party transfer exceptions. I attached our SCC template to reuse (SCC_template_Redwood_v2.pdf).
- DPIA: since this is a healthcare workload, recommend we include a short DPIA summary paragraph in the DPA and offer to share our DPIA artifacts under NDA if they need it.
- SOC 2: their security team may ask for control descriptions; the snapshot covers the most common requests. Keep the SOC2 snapshot internal; share only the summary link.

Operational impact: subprocessor cadence (quarterly + on-request) is fine. HIPAA/BAA: we'll treat BAAs as an addendum for covered workloads — need to document any technical controls required for covered data (encryption, access logging).

If legal is happy with counters, I can draft a short addendum language for the DPIA and BAAs.

— Karthik
